get.description: The kernel's health, for the load balancer and the smoke checks; no cookie is read.

post.description: A fresh copy of the Turner seed for whoever holds the passcode, and the owner cookie for it.
A fresh copy for an owner who already has one; the old copy is left as it is, and the cookie moves on.

get.description: The copy the owner cookie names.

The copy's businesses, each with its Desks, in the order the Desks were made: the Desk switcher. Each Desk
names its setup interview while that isn't finished.

post.description:
A new Desk in the owner's copy, made by the kernel with the owner's credential: for a new business, or for one
of the copy's businesses (`existing_business_id`, whose name, owner name and time zone it keeps). The kernel
activates the starter rules (every request asks, but for the utility tools) and refuses what a new Desk can't
have: a money cap, connected tools, an owner name outside its pattern, an unknown time zone or another copy's
business (404). Counts on the copy's `new_desk` limit (10 an hour).

delete.description:
Delete one of the copy's Desks, through the kernel with the owner's credential: its chats close, its public
page and links stop working, and it leaves the copy's Desks; its ledger is kept. A Desk of another copy, or one
already deleted, is 404 before anything is sent.

put.description:
The Answering switch, set by the kernel with the owner's credential. Off, visitors can only leave their
details or ask for a callback; the owner's own previews keep every tool.

The business the Desk belongs to: its name, the owner's name customers see, its time zone and brand, for every
Desk of that business.
What the Desk tells the public about the business (contact, service area, policies), in place of before.
The opening hours, in the business's time zone.
The price list, in place of before; quotes already given keep their amounts.
The bookable slots, in place of before; the kernel keeps a slot that is booked or waiting on a request.

People on record, upserted and removed by `ref`. Verification codes go only to a person's contact, so the
kernel refuses a contact that looks masked (as the owner is shown it) and keeps the one on record when `contact`
is null; its refusal is passed on as it is.

get.description:
The people on record, in the order they were added, each with the masked contact the kernel keeps for owners'
screens, and the leads visitors left, newest first, their names and notes as typed (untrusted text).

put.description: What alerts the owner at once and what waits for the briefing.

post.description:
A new chat on the Desk as a customer, for its owner: the kernel opens it with the owner's credential as a
visitor session marked `preview`, which keeps the visitor tools while Answering is off (setup's try-out before
going live). Its token goes only into the visitor cookie for the Desk's public routes, so the public chat then
runs as that session. Like any new chat it counts toward the address's `new_chat` limit.

get.description:
Today on the Desk, computed from the rows on each read (so polling never empties it): how many things need the
owner, the live conversations, the briefing since 18:00 yesterday and the last 7 days, in the business's time
zone.

Every briefing item since 18:00 yesterday in the business's time zone, newest first: the list Today's
briefing links to.

The last `days` local dates on the Desk, today included, in the business's time zone: bookings, the money
paid, and the conversations Claude handled alone versus the ones that needed the owner.
The Desk's conversations, the latest activity first; the owner's own previews included.

A conversation on one of the copy's Desks, as the owner sees it, after the cursor `after` (polled every 2 s).
The cursor never skips a row: a session's rows commit in the order of their `n`. `typing_until` is when the
visitor's typing dots stop, while they are typing (presence in this process's memory, never stored).
Status reasons are read concurrently with the owner's kernel credential, with bounded caching for final
execution refusals; an unreadable reason is null, so the stored transcript still renders.

The Desk's refused requests and Claude's stopped drafts, newest first. Today and Safety count refused requests
only (owner decision, 2026-10-31). Each refusal's nullable `cause` comes from its decision's `policy_ids` and
its ledger decide summary's `reason`/`check` and the session's verified state; drafts have no cause.

The copy's Demo inbox, read from the kernel with the owner's credential. Its bodies can hold verification
codes, so the answer is never stored, here or in a cache.

The Desk's signed ledger, verified by the kernel on every read (its chain, `first_bad_seq` and key), passed
on unchanged.

parameters.name: verify

schema.description: Always true: the kernel verifies every read
schema.title: Verify

parameters.description: Always true: the kernel verifies every read

get.description:
What waits for the owner on the Desk: each held request as the kernel has it now (read with the owner's
credential, which applies expiry), oldest first, then each open callback request.

post.description:
Mark a callback request done, through the kernel with the owner's credential. A handoff that isn't on one of
the copy's Desks is 404 and never sent. The kernel answers 409 `conflict` for one already done, and 409 `closed`
for one whose Desk was deleted after the copy's Desks were read; the route passes either on.

get.description:
A decision of the copy as the kernel signed it, read with the owner's credential (which applies expiry). One of
another copy is the kernel's 404; a decision the kernel answered for that isn't on one of the copy's Desks is 404
too, so no other copy's record is ever passed on.

post.description:
The owner's answer to a held request. The kernel decides it with the owner's credential, and an allow runs
there and then, as the visitor's session (also during a take-over); the visitor sees the signed approved status
before the outcome when the answer includes it, and Claude follows up once the resume job ran and the visitor's
own credential is present (the open stream or the next
request). Drafted rule cards come back in `card_diff`; proving them is a rules route's work, so an answer never
waits on a proof.

When the kernel refuses the answer (409: answered before, expired or cancelled) or its response is lost, the
decision is read as it stands: once it left `held` and `approved`, an outcome the visitor wasn't shown yet gets
the (idempotent) resume job, so a lost response still resumes the chat. While `approved`, publish its signed
receipt without waking Claude and leave a `decision_pending` row under the session's run lock. The visitor's
next request can then read its final outcome even if the first answer never queues a job. Either case answers
409 `already_resolved` with the decision. A decision still `held` keeps the kernel's own error, its code included
("Errors"): a 409 is
`{error: "kernel", code}`, and an answer that never reached the kernel is 503, `seed_unproved` and `internal`
kept. A decision that can't be read is 503 `kernel_unavailable`. In each case answering again is safe. An answer
the request doesn't offer is the kernel's 422 `invalid`.

Take the conversation over from Claude, or from a breaker pause, at the generation the owner last read: the
kernel moves it to mode `owner` (a new generation, so nothing Claude had in flight is shown), the visitor sees the
owner join by the kernel's name for them, and Claude reads that the owner took over at its next call. A stale
generation is the kernel's 409 `stale_generation`.

Hand a conversation the owner took over back to Claude, at the generation the owner last read: the kernel
moves it to mode `ai` (a new generation), the visitor sees the owner leave, and Claude reads that the owner handed
it back. Work that waited for the owner (an answered request's outcome, a whisper) wakes Claude, whose turn runs
with the visitor's credential once it is present: the open stream or the next request.

Resume a conversation the breaker paused, at the generation the owner last read: the kernel moves it back to
mode `ai` (a new generation, its strikes reset), and Claude reads that the owner resumed it. Work still waiting
wakes Claude as after a hand-back; work the pause's handoff already answered doesn't.

The owner's words in a conversation, through the kernel with the owner's credential (it ledgers both kinds).

A `say` goes to the visitor once the owner has taken the conversation over (else 409 `take_over_first`): the
kernel checks it and signs it at the session's generation, and only a passing verdict is shown, through
`deliver()`, as the owner's, with an `owner_say` row so Claude reads it at its next call. A say the kernel blocks
comes back to the owner unchanged and reaches no one; one the session moved past before it could be shown is 409
`stale_generation`. A `whisper` is a note for Claude alone, in any mode, held as untrusted text: in mode `ai` it
wakes Claude's next turn, which runs with the visitor's credential once it is present; during a take-over it
waits for the hand-back; during a breaker pause Claude reads it at its first call after the resume.

The owner is typing in a conversation they took over, at the generation they read: the visitor sees their
initials, name and three dots for five seconds, or until their say replaces them (an `owner_typing` event that
carries the kernel's name for the owner and when the dots stop, never text). Presence, not a message: no kernel
call but the one naming the owner, no ledger entry. In any other mode it is 409 `take_over_first`, and at a
generation the session has left 409 `stale_generation`. The app sends about one signal every two seconds while
the owner types, never one per keystroke: each one still costs a kernel call, database reads and a moment of the
conversation's lock. At most one event goes out every two seconds; a signal sooner changes nothing.

Start setting up a new Desk from the owner's own words: Claude reads them, the kernel makes the Desk with
Answering off, and Claude asks whether it may read the owner's Claude memory and website. A name the owner gives
here is the one customers see, and one the kernel wouldn't take is 422. 503 `model_unavailable` when Claude
couldn't answer, with nothing made.

Each start carries an `idempotency_key`, one per click (422 without one, as for any missing field). A repeat in
the copy answers the interview the first made, as it stands now, and makes nothing: no model call, no Desk, no
count on the limits. A repeat with another body is 409 `conflict`, and one sent while the first is still starting
answers 409 `in_progress` at once, to be sent again after `retry_after`. A first that stopped before the kernel
was asked for the Desk (its process did, say) frees the key once it is older than the longest a start can take. A
start is admitted (looked up, counted and claimed) under its key's lock in this process, so a repeat sent
meanwhile waits for that admission and is never counted; another process admits on its own, so during a deploy's
overlap a repeat routed to the other task can be counted twice.

409 `key_spent` (no `retry_after`) means this key is spent: its start asked the kernel for the Desk and then
failed, or stopped with no answer kept and is now older than the longest a start can take. The Desk may exist,
so the key never starts again and waiting changes nothing; a new click needs a new key. The first request still
answers its own failure.

A start that fails before the kernel is asked for the Desk (refused by the limits, or Claude couldn't answer)
frees its key, so the same request can be sent again. Once the Desk was asked for, the key keeps the outcome
whatever the kernel answered, a refusal too, and a repeat of a start that failed answers 409 `key_spent`.

get.description: The setup interview as it stands, removing abandoned turn entries and reopening consent if needed.

One owner turn's whole reply so far, then done once its state is saved and the interview takes the next turn,
or error after rollback.

No running turn sends done with run null immediately. Choices, cards and plans are read only
from the existing state route. Authentication and interview scoping finish before SSE starts.

post.description:
Use the shared turn runner to store consent, then read Claude memory and the named website through the
kernel on yes, or skip both on no. Claude's first question and the read labels land together. Wait for the
busy commit, then answer 202 `SetupState` with `busy: true` at once; the turn's events stream follows the
reads and Claude's opening, and the state route has the result. Cancelling the request leaves the run
working. A repeat while busy answers 202 without starting or counting another run; after it lands, consent
is 409 `conflict`. Failed or abandoned runs reopen consent.

Use the shared turn runner for the owner's answer to the question waiting, which the answer names
(409 `conflict` when none is waiting or another is, so an answer sent twice answers once). Claude replies,
updates the answers and asks the next question once this one is covered. Wait for the busy commit, then up to
25 seconds: 200 with the landed state or 202 `SetupState` with `busy: true`. Any turn while busy answers 202
without running or counting on the limits. Cancelling the request leaves the turn working. Failure or
abandonment removes the staged answer and leaves the same question waiting, so the owner can retry.
503 `model_unavailable` when Claude couldn't answer or the run deadline expires.
Answer the waiting proposal and receive Claude's reply and next ask.
Use the current proposals and finish questions with safe defaults for unanswered limits.

get.description: The new Desk's tools, and the mock payments server while it isn't connected.

post.description:
Connect the mock payments server (test mode, no money moves) before the rules are confirmed: its tools come
back pinned and waiting for the owner's review. 409 `conflict` once the rules are confirmed.

get.description:
Read nonblank public lines in board order, hours and prices, with their provenance.
Allowed at `rules` or `situations`; 409 `conflict` at any other step or while a turn is pending.

put.description:
Edit one public line and strictly publish the charter before saving its owner provenance.
Allowed at `rules` or `situations`, without changing the step; 409 `conflict` otherwise. Every write publishes
the confirmed lines and leaves out held lines (`held`), values still suggested, and every policy line while
setup's policy claims are switched off; a rewording that is published clears its line's hold. A refused charter
is 422 `line_refused`, naming the refused key and reason codes when available; a charter cap names no key.
`policy:how_we_help` is 422 `not_editable`. A failed save restores the stored charter once, then answers 409.

409.description: A stale item id, an unavailable setup step, an active turn or a failed save returns `error: conflict`. A kernel part conflict returns `error: kernel`, `code: conflict`, after attempting repair of sent parts.

schema.title: Response 422 Owner Setup Put Public Line

post.description:
Confirm only the listed keys at the displayed revision; publish before saving without changing the step.
Allowed at `rules` or `situations`; 409 `conflict` otherwise. A stale revision is 409 `conflict`, checked before
the keys, so a key removed since the owner's view isn't an invalid request. A refused charter is 422
`line_refused`, naming the refused key and reason codes when available; a charter cap names no key. A held key
is 422 `line_refused` naming it, with nothing changed: only a rewording can publish it. A failed save restores
the stored parts once, then answers 409. Blank lines and empty hours or prices remain unconfirmed.

409.description: A stale item id, an unavailable setup step, an active turn or a failed save returns `error: conflict`. A kernel part conflict returns `error: kernel`, `code: conflict`, after attempting repair of sent parts.

schema.title: Response 422 Owner Setup Confirm Public Lines

409.description: A stale item id, an unavailable setup step, an active turn or a failed save returns `error: conflict`. A kernel part conflict returns `error: kernel`, `code: conflict`, after attempting repair of sent parts.

schema.title: Response 422 Owner Setup Delete Public Line

delete.description:
Remove one suggested price only when its current id, title and amount match what the owner saw.
Owner prices are 422 `not_suggested`; a missing or mismatched item is 409 `conflict`.
Allowed at `rules` or `situations`, under the same turn guard, publication and repair as edits.

409.description: A stale item id, an unavailable setup step, an active turn or a failed save returns `error: conflict`. A kernel part conflict returns `error: kernel`, `code: conflict`, after attempting repair of sent parts.

schema.title: Response 422 Owner Setup Delete Public Price

get.description:
The Desk's public page: the kernel's `PublicDesk`, unchanged. Never cached: the page's open status refetches
on a delay that assumes a fresh answer (CloudFront doesn't cache `/api/*` either).

Where agents send their requests and how they sign them, built by code from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, never from the
request's own host headers. The kernel's public Desk is read only to answer 404 for an unknown slug.

post.description:
The visitor's session on the slug's Desk: the one the cookie holds while the kernel says it is open there (a
returning visitor), else a new one, whose token only the cookie holds. Resuming is never limited, however often a
page reloads (it creates nothing), and is ledgered as a `session` event at most once per session every ten
minutes; a new chat counts toward `new_chat`.

get.description:
The session's state and its transcript as the visitor sees it: their own words, what was delivered to them
and where the owner joined and left, never model, note, owner-only or other sessions' rows.

The items, `last_seq` and then the state (the session's kernel_ro row) are read in one snapshot. The kernel
commits a take-over or a hand-back before the API writes its event, so the state holds every change whose event
`last_seq` covers, and a later change's event comes past it: the event stream opened after `last_seq` neither
misses nor repeats an item, and agrees with the state it starts from. The mode `GET /whoami` answered with is
older and could predate a hand-back whose event `last_seq` covers. A session closed by then, or no longer the
kernel's, is 401 `no_session`, which clears the cookie.

post.description:
Store the visitor's message and start Claude's turn; the answer arrives on the event stream.

Every message counts toward the post limit, in every mode, and one that starts a model turn (mode `ai`) toward the
turn limits too, per conversation and per address; past any of them it is refused before anything is stored,
checked or woken. Then what control rows left for this session is done first, so an outcome that came in
meanwhile precedes the message and the same turn answers both. The message wakes a turn unless the owner has taken
the chat over (mode `owner`: the owner answers it). In a paused session that turn is the kernel's handoff, with no
model call: it runs under the session's turn lock and stops the waiting work from starting more turns, so one
handoff answers the message and whatever else was waiting. Neither counts toward the turn limits. Once the message
is stored, its translation for the owner is queued (Plan 02b, Task 10), unless the chat is paused or the
conversation's `translate` limit is spent; a queue that can't take it changes nothing here.

The visitor is typing: the owner's view of the conversation shows their dots for five seconds (Plan 02b).
Presence, not a message: it carries no text, stores nothing and calls the kernel only to name the session. The
page sends about one signal every two seconds while the visitor types, never one per keystroke: each one still
costs a kernel call and database reads. A signal within two seconds of the last one that counted changes nothing,
and nothing here is ever shown to the visitor or to Claude.

get.description:
The session's events after the cursor, then live ones (SSE `id` is the event's `seq`). On opening, and as each
control row appears while it is open, the session's runner does what control rows left and runs waiting work,
with the visitor's credential, in a task of its own: a hang-up never cuts it short. Three streams per session
and thirty per address may be open at once: a session's fourth closes its oldest (opening a stream is never
refused for its session's streams, so a reload never is), and past the address's thirty it is 429. A closed
stream ends even while its client has stopped reading, and its place is freed once it has ended, however it
ended.

post.description:
Withdraw one of the visitor's own held requests. The kernel cancels it (409 once it is no longer held, 404
for another session's); its signed outcome is then shown as `resolved`, and Claude reads it at the next turn
(an `action_update` that starts none: the visitor already sees what happened).

Ask for a code for the contact the visitor typed. The kernel sends it only to the contact on record, as a Demo
inbox entry, and answers with one message whether or not the contact is on record; the visitor's stream gets the
entry's code-free notice. Owner alerts never reach the visitor, here or on the stream.

The code the visitor typed into the verify card, checked by the kernel; it is never stored, logged, streamed or
shown to Claude. A wrong, expired or used-up code is the kernel's 422 `{"error": "kernel", "code": "invalid"}`,
and a code that isn't six digits 422 `{"error": "invalid"}`: the card shows one message for both. Once the session
is verified, a note tells Claude (it wakes a turn, which gets the verified tools).

get.description:
The session's Demo inbox, read from the kernel with the visitor's credential: the codes sent for the
verifications this session started, never an owner alert. Its bodies hold codes, so the answer is never stored,
here or in a cache.

post.description:
A demo key for connecting an agent of the visitor's own: its key ID, its Ed25519 private key and a spending
limit the demo wallet signed, which the agent sends when it opens its session at the A2A endpoint. The key is
handed over in this answer once and kept nowhere, here or in a cache. Five demo agents a copy an hour, this and
sending the built-in one together.

get.description:
Which words the built-in agent's tasks take on the visitor's Desk, the set its first message comes from
(`agents.demo_task_set`): the business type setup stored for the Desk, or Turner's on the copy's own Desk. A key
the page words its task chips by, never text of the Desk's. The ordered tasks fit the Desk's enabled tools.
Read with the visitor's session; never cached.

post.description:
Send the built-in visiting agent, Alex Kim's assistant, to the Desk on one of the demo tasks; it runs in this
process and talks to the Desk through the public A2A endpoint. Poll its run each second with the ID answered
here. Five demo agents a copy an hour; 503 `demo_budget` once today's model budget is spent.

Each send carries an `idempotency_key`, one per click (422 without one, as for any missing field). A repeat in
the copy within the hour answers the run the first started (its ID; poll it for its state) and starts nothing, and
a repeat that finds the key never counts on the limit. One with another task, or from another session or to
another Desk than the key's, is 409 `conflict`. The key is claimed once the limit and the budget let the request
through, before the kernel mints the agent. A request is admitted (looked up, counted and claimed) under its key's
lock in this process, so a repeat sent meanwhile waits for that admission, then answers the run; another process
admits on its own, so during a deploy's overlap a repeat routed to the other task can be counted twice. Keys live
in this process's memory, like the runs, each for its run's hour; while 1000 are held, a new one is 429
`rate_limited` until the oldest one's hour ends.

A request that fails before anything is made (refused by the limit or the budget, or the kernel refused to mint the
agent with a 4xx) frees its key, so the same request can be sent again. Once the kernel may have minted the agent
(no answer came back, or a 5xx) or the run started, the key keeps the run however it ends, a failed one too, and a
new click sends a new key.

The agent's task is the fixed line of the Desk's set (`agents.demo_task_set`: its setup business type, or Turner's
for the copy's own Desk), read before anything is claimed.

get.description:
The built-in agent's run as it stands, for the session that sent it (any other is 404): each message the agent
sent, exactly as sent, as the agent's own untrusted words, and what the Desk answered, as the kernel checked it.
Kept for an hour. Never cached: a Desk turn can carry a payment link.

The document a link card opens, once: the kernel's bytes and content type. The tab shows it only when its type
can't run script (a PDF, a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image, plain text); any other is downloaded as an attachment,
sandboxed. A link that was opened, has expired or names nothing answers 404 `link_used_or_expired` alike. A
browser's prefetch or prerender is 503 `prefetch` with `Retry-After: 0`, and leaves the link unopened. Refusals
read as static copy unless JSON is asked for (`document_refusal`).
What the checkout page shows: the kernel's `PaymentLinkView`, unchanged. Never cached: the link's state moves.

post.description:
Pay the link (a test payment: no money moves). The kernel pays an `issued` link once and answers with its
`payment_confirmed` verdict, which is shown in the link's chat (`_confirm_in_chat`); any other link is 409 with how
it stands now, and nothing is shown.
Cancel an `issued` link at checkout: nothing is paid and there is no verdict; any other link is 409.

An agent's request to the Desk, signed with its key over `{desk_slug, ts, nonce, body_sha256}` (the Agent
Card says how). The answer is what the Desk showed since the agent's last answer, Claude's reply last; a request
sent again with the same nonce gets the answer its first try got and runs nothing.

The new Desk's first rules: its hours, prices, calendar and public details go to the kernel, Claude drafts rule
cards from the owner's answers (the template cards when its draft can't be used), and the kernel compiles and
proves them. Sent again, it re-posts the same cards and never drafts again. 409 `rules_cannot_be_checked` when
the kernel couldn't check them ("Rules can't be checked right now"); 409 `conflict` before the questions are
done or once the rules are confirmed.

Six situations Claude writes from the owner's answers, each tried against the drafted rules without running
anything, with whether the rules do what the owner would want. 409 `conflict` without a draft.

What a bad actor would try against the drafted rules, each with the kernel's verdict, run nowhere. 409
`conflict` without a draft.

Activate the drafted rules, with Answering still off, so the owner can try the Desk before it goes live. When
the rules changed after the draft, the same cards are drafted again and the answer is 409
`rules_changed_since_draft` with the new `draft` to confirm; 409 `conflict` without a proved draft.

Turn Answering on once the rules are confirmed (409 `conflict` before): the Desk answers the public at
`public_url`.

get.description:
The Desk's active rules: the version in force (its money cap is the Desk's), each tool with the cards that
cover it (its own, those on its effects, and the compiler's default ask where nothing else does) and its status,
and the preset the owner cards are, if exactly one.

One of the Desk's drafts, read again as it was made (its cards, money cap, proof and summary), with how it
differs from the active rules now. A version that isn't a draft of the Desk's is 404.

Rules the owner's own approvals suggest: a tool they approved at least 3 times in the last 30 days that no
auto card covers, with the card that would let Claude handle it ("You approved 3 quote requests. Let me handle
these?"). Drafting one is `POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/suggestions/{tool}`.

The tool's recent decisions on the Desk, for its page: newest first, `limit` at a time, the next page from
`before` (the last page's `next_before`). A tool the Desk doesn't have is 404.

post.description:
Connect the mock payments server (test mode, no money moves) to the Desk: its tools come back pinned by their
definition's hash and `needs_review`, so no one is given them until the owner reviews them; a tool already
connected is left as it is.

The demo's "Simulate a tool change": the mock payments server changes the connected tool's definition for this
copy, and the kernel finds it at once, so the tool needs the owner's review before Claude uses it again (its
changed definition is pending, as untrusted text). The kernel refuses a native tool (422).

get.description:
The owner's knowledge on this Desk, oldest first by `created_at`, null timestamps first, ties by `item_id`.
Content the kernel's read-only view masks stays null; listing never writes or asks the kernel for masked text.

post.description:
Tell Claude something about the business, kept by the kernel under its `item_id` (posting it again replaces
it): owner-only, or public once the owner marks it so (`Label(readers=["public"])`). It is information for Claude,
never a rule; the kernel refuses other readers or a text over 100 KiB (422), and keeps an item that quotes a
private document owner-only.

Add a document to the Desk, the owner's alone or a customer's on record (`record_owner_ref`). The kernel keeps
its text, which only a single-use link releases to that verified customer, and refuses one naming no one on
record (422).

Ask Claude about the Desk's rules in plain words. A question gets an answer and drafts nothing; a change comes
back as a draft the kernel compiled and proved, with how it differs from the active rules, which nothing changes
until `confirm`. Counts on the copy's `owner_ai` limit (40 an hour) and, in production, the daily model budget
(503 `demo_budget`); 503 `model_unavailable` when Claude couldn't answer.

Accept: text/event-stream subscribes to whole-answer deltas, reset on retry, then final
RuleChatOut after any kernel proof, or an error: the JSON error body this route would answer,
plus its status. Admission failures remain JSON. Without that header the existing JSON/202
behavior is unchanged.

Draft owner cards for the kernel to compile and prove: `cards` as they should stand, on the version they were
read from (`expected_parent`), or cards to `add` to the active ones, such as an approval's `card_diff` (one with an
active card's ID takes its place). The answer is the draft with its cards and how they differ from the active
rules; nothing changes until `confirm`. 409 `rules_cannot_be_checked` when the kernel couldn't check them.

Draft a preset in place of the Desk's owner cards: "Ask me first for everything" (`ask_first`) or "Recommended
rules" (`auto`). Every owner card goes, those for one person and "never" ones included, and the draft's diff lists
each; nothing changes until `confirm`.

Draft the card a suggestion offers for `tool`, added to the active owner cards; 404 when the owner's approvals
suggest nothing for it now. Nothing changes until `confirm`.

Draft the active rules at a new money cap, the most Claude takes or pays out in one action without asking:
lowering it brings each rule that takes or pays out more on its own down to it (asking instead at $0), each saying
its new limit, and the draft's diff lists them; raising it changes no rule. The draft is at the new cap, which
becomes the Desk's only when the owner confirms it. 422 `above_platform_ceiling` above the $10,000 ceiling, with
nothing drafted.

Send the owner's reviewed pins to the kernel. Enabling drafts a rules version; only explicit policy
confirmation activates it. Disabling takes effect immediately. A slow proof answers 202 with this request.

Activate a draft the owner read: its cards, and its money cap, become the Desk's. 409
`rules_changed_since_draft` when the rules changed after the draft (draft again from the rules now in force), 409
`conflict` for a draft the kernel didn't prove, 404 for a version that isn't one of the Desk's.

A2AError.title: A2AError
A2AError.description: An A2A error answer's body (Plan 02b, "Errors"): what went wrong, and that the answer comes from an AI.

AboveMoneyCap.title: AboveMoneyCap
AboveMoneyCap.description:
422 from a drafting route: a new or changed card would take or pay out more on its own than the Desk's money
cap, `cap_cents` (0 when unset), so nothing was drafted ("That's above your limit of $X. Raise the limit
first.").

AgentCardOut.title: AgentCardOut
AgentCardOut.description:
`GET /api/public/desks/{slug}/agent_card`: built by code from `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` and the slug, with no model
text; what agents may do here, and the AI disclosure, are the kernel's `PublicDesk.agent_card`.

AgentCardSigning.title: AgentCardSigning
AgentCardSigning.description: How an agent signs each request: the headers it sends and the payload its Ed25519 signature covers.

AgentRunStarted.title: AgentRunStarted
AgentRunStarted.description: 202: the built-in agent is on its way; poll `GET .../send_agent/{run_id}` for its run (Plan 02b).

AgentTasks.title: AgentTasks
AgentTasks.description:
Which words the built-in agent's tasks take on the Desk (plan 09, C2): `rivera` on the copy's own Desk, else
the business type setup stored for it (`other` without one). Tasks are listed in page order; the payment tasks
need an enabled agent payment tool. Keys, never words: the page holds every word.

AgentTurn.title: AgentTurn
AgentTurn.description:
One side of an exchange in a built-in agent's run: the agent's request (`n`-th), or the Desk's answer to it,
with the blocks and signed statuses the kernel checked and the Desk showed the agent.

An agent turn's `text` is the message the agent sent the Desk in that request, exactly as signed and sent (at most
2,000 characters, the agent's send limit), shown to the visitor who launched it as a visitor's own message is
(owner decision, 2026-11-01). The agent's model writes it from a fixed task line that code picks from signed
templates, keyed by the Desk's setup business type, with no owner or visitor text, and the Desk's kernel-checked
replies alone, and the kernel doesn't check it. It is untrusted plain text, the agent's words and never the
Desk's: the page shows it quoted and labelled as the agent's. A Desk turn's `text` is null; the Desk's replies stay the kernel-checked
blocks and statuses.

AlreadyResolved.title: AlreadyResolved
AlreadyResolved.description:
409: the request was no longer waiting for an answer (answered before, expired or cancelled); `decision` is
how it stands now, as the kernel signed it.

AnsweringIn.title: AnsweringIn
AnsweringIn.description:
`PUT /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/answering`: the Answering switch. Off, visitors can only leave their details
or ask for a callback.

ApiError.title: ApiError

ApprovalAnswerIn.title: ApprovalAnswerIn
ApprovalAnswerIn.description: `POST /api/owner/approvals/{decision_id}/answer`: one of the four answers to a held request.

ApprovalAnswerOut.title: ApprovalAnswerOut
ApprovalAnswerOut.description:
The answered request as the kernel signed it, how its execution went (an allow runs inside the answer; None
for a denial or a request the rules no longer allow), and the rule cards an `allow_person` or `deny_always`
answer drafts, which the owner proves and confirms through the rules routes (Plan 02b).

Attempt.title: Attempt
Attempt.description:
A Safety entry (`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/safety`): a refused decision (`ref_id` its
`decision_id`) or a reply of Claude's it blocked (`ref_id` the reply entry's `seq`, as text). `reason_plain` is the
kernel's owner text for a decision, or a line the API composes for a reply; `origin` is the ledger entry's;
`ledger_seq` is the entry to show it with. `triage` is AI-written, when there is one (Plan 02b). `cause` is a
closed code for a refused request, from the decision's `policy_ids`, its ledger summary's `reason`/`check`
and the session's verified state;
the web holds its words. It is null for held requests, stopped drafts and unmapped refusals.

Briefing.title: Briefing
Briefing.description:
"Since last night": from 18:00 yesterday in the business's time zone (`since`) to now. `answers` counts the
list's `answer` items, the conversations Claude answered alone; `total` is the length of the full list
(`BriefingList`).

BriefingItem.title: BriefingItem
BriefingItem.description:
One thing that happened since last night. `ref_id` is what it links to: the refused decision for `turned_down`,
the decision for a booking, the `lead_id`, the session for an answer. `line` is the kernel's owner text for a
refusal or a booking, a lead's note (untrusted, as the visitor or Claude wrote it), else None. `cause` is required
and nullable: the refused request's closed cause code for `turned_down`, null for other kinds and unmapped
refusals. Stopped drafts stay on Safety and out of the briefing.

BriefingList.title: BriefingList
BriefingList.description: `GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/briefing`: every item since last night, newest first.

BriefingNewest.title: BriefingNewest
BriefingNewest.description: The newest refused request, booking, and lead or answer (the lead when both share a time); None when none.

BusinessOut.title: BusinessOut
BusinessOut.description: `GET /api/owner/desks`: one of the copy's businesses, with its Desks (the Desk switcher).

CancelAccepted.title: CancelAccepted
CancelAccepted.description: 202: the held request is withdrawn; its outcome arrives on the event stream as `resolved`.

CardDiff.title: CardDiff
CardDiff.description:
How a draft's cards differ from the active version's, by `card_id`, default cards left out; `changed` pairs
each card before and after.

ChangesAlwaysOn.title: ChangesAlwaysOn
ChangesAlwaysOn.description:
422 from a drafting route: the cards named in `card_ids`, in the draft's order, would change starting a
verification, which is always on (codes go only to the contact on record, under the built-in rule), so nothing
was drafted.

CheckedDraft.title: CheckedDraft
CheckedDraft.description: A reply of Claude's exactly as it was sent to the kernel's reply check: its prose and its clauses.

ConfirmRulesIn.title: ConfirmRulesIn
ConfirmRulesIn.description: `POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/confirm`: the drafted version the owner read and confirms.

why.title: Why
why.description: Why this helps, at most 200 characters.

ConversationSummary.title: ConversationSummary
ConversationSummary.description:
A conversation on the Desk: who it is with (`display_name` as `NeedsYouSession`'s), who has it (`mode`), when
anything last happened in it, how its requests stand (decisions by state), and whether it is the owner's own
preview. `latest_visitor_text` is the newest message the visitor typed, untrusted text shown as typed, with its
whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces and trimmed, and cut to 199 characters and "…" when longer than 200;
never Claude's words. It is null for an agent's conversation, the owner's preview and a visitor who hasn't
written yet. `latest_outcome` is the newest decisive event, derived from stored events, never task names, prose
or positive counts; otherwise null. An agent's is an executed booking/mandate charge with its matching shown,
checked done card and executed receipt in the same turn, or a Desk-authored payment confirmation; an actual
refusal at decide/execution gives `turned_down`, and a later hold or handoff clears success. A visitor's (never
the owner's preview) comes from the kernel's decisions, payment links and handoffs alone, timed by their ledger
entries: an executed quote (`quoted`), booking (`visit_booked`), lead (`lead_captured`) or document release
(`document_sent`), a payment link paid (`deposit_paid`), a refusal at decide/execution (`turned_down`), the
owner declining a held request (`owner_declined`), or a call-back the owner marked done (`called_back`); a later
request still held, expired or cancelled, or a handoff card opening, clears it to null.

CopyOut.title: CopyOut
CopyOut.description: The owner's copy: what `POST /api/owner/copies`, `start_over` and `me` answer with.

CoveringCard.title: CoveringCard
CoveringCard.description:
A card of the active rules that covers a tool: its own (`shared` false), or one on an effect the tool has, which
every tool with that effect shares. A default card is the compiler's ask for a tool no card for anyone covers.

DemoAgentRun.title: DemoAgentRun
DemoAgentRun.description:
`GET /api/public/desks/{slug}/send_agent/{run_id}`: a built-in agent's run as its launcher's panel shows it,
kept in the process's memory for an hour (Plan 02b).

DeskSetup.title: DeskSetup
DeskSetup.description:
A Desk's setup interview that hasn't gone live: its ID (`GET /api/owner/setup/{id}`) and the step it is at.
Setup finishes at its go-live step (step `live`); an interview whose rules are confirmed but that hasn't gone live
(`preview`) is still unfinished, since going live is setup's last step.

DeskSummary.title: DeskSummary
DeskSummary.description:
One of the copy's Desks. `setup` is its setup interview while that isn't finished, so the owner can go back
into it; null once its setup interview went live (setup's go-live step) and for a Desk made outside setup.
`answering` is separate: the Answering switch can turn a Desk on before its setup finishes, and it still lists its
setup.

DocumentIn.title: DocumentIn
DocumentIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/documents`: a document for the Desk, the owner's alone or a customer's on
record (`record_owner_ref`), released only through the kernel's single-use links.

DraftAddIn.title: DraftAddIn
DraftAddIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/draft`: cards to add to the active owner cards, such as an approval's
`card_diff`; a card with the ID of an active one takes its place. Each card is bounded as `DraftCardsIn`'s are,
and so is the Desk's count of owner cards once these are added: beyond any bound, 422 `invalid`.

DraftCardsIn.title: DraftCardsIn
DraftCardsIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/draft`: the owner cards as they should stand, on the version they were read
from (the kernel answers 409 `conflict` once another is active). At most 60 cards (default asks need not be
sent: the kernel adds its own), each `card_id` at most 128 characters and each `reason` at most 200, as a rules
chat writes them; beyond any of these, 422 `invalid`. A card the kernel drafted for one person or agent from an
approval keeps its reason as the kernel wrote it, however long the name it quotes.

GenerationIn.title: GenerationIn
GenerationIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/conversations/{session_id}/{takeover,handback,resume,typing}`: the session's generation as the
owner last read it; a change made at a generation the session has since left is refused.

Handoff.title: Handoff
Handoff.description:
A conversation handed to the owner (`kernel_ro.handoffs`), of one of two kinds:

- `callback`: a visitor's call-back request. `reason` is "<name> · <contact> · <reason>" as the visitor typed them
  (untrusted text); `callback_window` is "<start>/<end>" in ISO 8601, or None without one.
- `card`: the handoff card the session saw (a passed reply citing it, or a blocked final draft or one no rewrite
  fixes). `reason` is the kernel's own template ("The Desk handed this to you."), and `callback_window` is None:
  no call back was promised.

A null window alone can't tell them apart; `kind` does, and a row's kind never changes. A card handoff opens
none in the owner's preview, while a held request awaits the owner, or while the session has an open handoff. A
call-back request closes the session's open card handoff (it reads `done` from then on) and opens its own
`callback` row with a new ID.

HealthOut.title: HealthOut
HealthOut.description: `GET /api/health`: 200 with the kernel's health, or 503 with `ok` false and no kernel field.

questions.title: Questions
questions.description: 1 to 5 intake questions, each 1 to 120 characters.

who.title: Who
who.description: Who this is for, at most 60 characters; empty if unclear.

why.title: Why
why.description: Why this helps, at most 200 characters.

how.title: How
how.description: How the Desk helps, at most 300 characters.

KnowledgeIn.title: KnowledgeIn
KnowledgeIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/knowledge`: something the owner tells Claude about the business (untrusted
text, never policy), owner-only (`Label(readers=["owner"])`) or public (`Label(readers=["public"])`); posting an
item again under its `item_id` replaces it, so marking one public is posting it with the public label.

KnowledgeRow.title: KnowledgeRow
KnowledgeRow.description:
An owner-only read of `kernel_ro.knowledge_items`. `title` and `text` are null exactly when the view
masks them for a kernel-forced owner-only item. `created_at` is when it was first added, null for legacy rows
without a timestamp. Every field is always sent.

Lead.title: Lead
Lead.description: Details a visitor left: the name and note as they typed them (untrusted text, either may be missing).

MessageAccepted.title: MessageAccepted
MessageAccepted.description: 202: the visitor's message is stored; Claude's answer arrives on the event stream.

MoneyCapIn.title: MoneyCapIn
MoneyCapIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/money_cap`: the money cap to draft the active rules at, the most an auto rule
may take or pay out in one action without asking, in cents: from 0 (every payment asks) to the $10,000 platform
ceiling. Above the ceiling, 422 `above_platform_ceiling`; anything but a whole number of cents from 0, 422
`invalid`.

NeedsYouItem.title: NeedsYouItem
NeedsYouItem.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/needs_you`: a held request (`decision`, as the kernel signed it when read, which
applies expiry, with `held_by`, the reason of the rule card that held it, and `held_at`, when it was decided) or
an open handoff (`handoff`: a call-back request or the handoff card's), never both; who it came from; what they
wrote last (`from_the_visitor`: their previous and last messages, each a one-line glimpse of at most 200
characters, joined with " · "; their own untrusted words); and, on a handoff only, the conversation's newest
AI-written triage summary (`claude_summary`: what the person asked for and what the Desk did, for the owner alone,
shown as "Claude's note on what the Desk stopped: {summary}" and never quoted as the visitor's), else None. A held
request asks the owner for a decision, so neither it nor a handoff in a session with one awaiting the owner carries
AI-written text: a visitor could steer a summary to sway an approval.

NeedsYouSession.title: NeedsYouSession
NeedsYouSession.description:
Who a held request or a callback request came from. `display_name` is the verified person's, else the name
the session's lead gave (untrusted text), else None.

OwnerMessageIn.title: OwnerMessageIn
OwnerMessageIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/conversations/{session_id}/messages`: the owner's words, said to the visitor once the owner has
taken the conversation over (`say`), or a private note for Claude (`whisper`).

OwnerTranscript.title: OwnerTranscript
OwnerTranscript.description:
`GET /api/owner/conversations/{session_id}?after=n`: the session's state and its transcript after the cursor, as
the owner sees it (agent text, whispers, translations and triage included; model, note and context rows never).
`typing_until` is when the visitor's typing dots stop, while the visitor is typing, else null (Plan 02b): presence,
kept in the API's memory and shown to the owner alone.

owner_plain.title: Owner Plain
owner_plain.description: Owner-only execution refusal reason for this exact status, fetched with the owner's credential; never part of the stored or signed visitor event.

OwnerTranscriptItem.title: OwnerTranscriptItem
OwnerTranscriptItem.description:
The owner's view adds the AI-written translation and triage (Plan 02b), which never reach a visitor, and each
draft of Claude's the reply check stopped.
`owner_plain` is always present: the owner-only reason for this exact execution refusal, or null.

`cursor` is where the item stands for `after`: its own `n`, or later once a translation or triage was written onto
it, when the item comes again with the same `n` (replace it) and the later cursor (advance `after` to the largest
one read). Items come in transcript order (`n`), each once per read.

A `stopped_draft` item (Plan 02b) stands where the check stopped the draft, before the rewrite or the handoff that
followed: its `stopped_draft` holds the draft and why it was stopped, and it has no `text` or `event`. Every other
item's `stopped_draft` is null.

PaymentConflict.title: PaymentConflict
PaymentConflict.description:
409 from the checkout's complete or cancel: the link is no longer `issued`. `state` is how it reads now and
`cancel_reason` why it was cancelled, `rules_changed` when a rule change cancelled it, so the checkout page can say
so (master plan, "Payment links").

PeopleOut.title: PeopleOut
PeopleOut.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/people`: the people on record, in the order they were added, and the leads,
newest first.

PersonOnRecord.title: PersonOnRecord
PersonOnRecord.description: Someone on record on the Desk. Verification codes go only to their contact, which leaves the kernel masked.

PresetIn.title: PresetIn
PresetIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/preset`: "Ask me first for everything" (`ask_first`) or "Recommended rules"
(`auto`).

ProvingPending.title: ProvingPending
ProvingPending.description:
202: the rules are still being drafted or checked. Send `retry` again in a few seconds: it picks up the same
work, or its answer once done.

ProvingRetry.title: ProvingRetry
ProvingRetry.description: The request to send again, unchanged: its path and its JSON body (None when it has none).

RecordedHistory.title: RecordedHistory
RecordedHistory.description:
Which of Today's sections count recorded history: the night the kernel replayed into the copy when it was made
(Plan 01d), which the owner's screens label "Includes recorded history". A replay holds only finished things, so
`needs_you` stays false; it keeps the shape the web reads.

Reports.title: Reports
Reports.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/reports?days=n`: the last `n` local dates in the business's time zone, today
included, counted as Today's "Last 7 days" is. `bookings` are the bookings made; `paid_cents` the money paid,
through payment links and agents' spending limits; `handled_by_claude` and `needed_you` split the conversations
into those Claude handled alone and those the owner stepped into. `recorded_history` is true when any of these
counts includes the night the kernel replayed into the copy (as `RecordedHistory` is for Today).

RuleChatIn.title: RuleChatIn
RuleChatIn.description: `POST /api/owner/policy/{desk_id}/chat`: what the owner asks Claude about the rules, in their own words.

RuleChatOut.title: RuleChatOut
RuleChatOut.description:
Claude's reply to the owner (AI-written, owner-facing) and, when they asked for a change, the draft the kernel
compiled and proved; None for a question, with nothing drafted.

RulesChanged.title: RulesChanged
RulesChanged.description:
409 from a confirm: the rules changed after the draft was made, so the same cards were drafted again on the
rules now in force, and `draft` is the new version to read and confirm.

RulesDraft.title: RulesDraft
RulesDraft.description:
A rules version the kernel compiled and proved, for the owner to read and confirm: its owner cards (default
asks left out), how they differ from the active version's (None in setup), the money cap its money cards are held
to, the kernel's proof, and a summary.

RulesSummary.title: RulesSummary
RulesSummary.description: A draft's cards in the owner's words: each card's reason, by what it does (once each).

RulesView.title: RulesView
RulesView.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/rules`: the active rules version, each tool of the Desk with the cards that
cover it, and the preset the active owner cards are, if they are exactly one (else None: there is no "custom"
state).

SafetyCheck.title: SafetyCheck
SafetyCheck.description:
`POST /api/owner/policy/setup/{id}/safety_check`: what a bad actor would try against the drafted rules,
run nowhere. `total` counts the rows tried (one lacking a stand-in price is left out), `blocked` those stopped, and
`seconds` how long the kernel took.

SafetyRow.title: SafetyRow
SafetyRow.description:
One thing a bad actor would try (`label`, and `tries`, what they'd say), the kernel's verdict on it against
the drafted rules (its outcome and `reason_plain`, shown verbatim), and whether it was stopped: refused, or held
for the owner where that stops it, and never when it depends on the reviewer agreeing.

SetupAnswerIn.title: SetupAnswerIn
SetupAnswerIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/setup/{id}/answer`: the owner's text and exactly one waiting question or card id.
Naming the ask prevents a repeated answer from answering the next one.

SetupConsentIn.title: SetupConsentIn
SetupConsentIn.description: `POST /api/owner/setup/{id}/consent`: whether Claude may read the owner's Claude memory and website.

SetupMessage.title: SetupMessage
SetupMessage.description:
One line of the setup conversation, owner-facing: Claude's, the owner's, or an inline label for a read of the
owner's memory or website (`tool_label`). Choices belong only to a Claude question with choices; a card belongs
only to a card message, with role `claude` and empty text.

SetupProposalIn.title: SetupProposalIn
SetupProposalIn.description: The owner's decision on a setup proposal, with optional changes when accepting it.

SetupPublicLine.title: SetupPublicLine
SetupPublicLine.description:
A nonblank setup charter line and whether the owner has confirmed its text. `held` marks a line the kernel's
public-text checks held back (the setup state's `held_policy_keys`, the contact included): its stored words stay
off the charter until the owner rewords it.

SetupStartIn.title: SetupStartIn
SetupStartIn.description:
`POST /api/owner/setup`: the owner's own words about the business, the business's time zone (an IANA name)
and, if they give it, the name customers should see for them, which wins over one taken from the words. A name
the owner types is used as typed (extra spaces aside), so it must fit the kernel's owner name pattern (letters,
spaces, apostrophes and hyphens, up to 40), else 422 before Claude is asked. The `idempotency_key`, one per click
and required (422 without one), makes a repeat answer the interview the first made instead of making another.

held_policy_keys.title: Held Policy Keys
held_policy_keys.description: Charter claim keys, such as a policy line or the public contact, withheld by the kernel's public-text checks; empty when nothing was held at the latest charter write.

SetupState.title: SetupState
SetupState.description:
A setup interview as it stands: its Desk, made at the start with Answering off, the step it is at, whether the
owner let Claude read their memory and website (None until asked), the question waiting for an answer (None
before consent, while busy and after the last one; `test_client` while the test-client offer at the plan's end
waits), whether an owner turn is pending (`busy`), and the conversation so far. Its messages start at Claude's
consent question: the owner's opening description isn't shown back to them.

SetupSuggestionsIn.title: SetupSuggestionsIn
SetupSuggestionsIn.description: Finish setup questions with the current suggestions; no additional answers are supplied.

SetupTools.title: SetupTools
SetupTools.description:
`GET /api/owner/setup/{id}/tools`: the new Desk's tools, and the connection it can still add (the
mock payments server, until it is connected).

SimulateChangeIn.title: SimulateChangeIn
SimulateChangeIn.description: `POST /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/tools/simulate_change`: the connected tool whose definition the demo changes.

Situation.title: Situation
Situation.description:
A situation Claude wrote to try against the drafted rules: who brings it, the probe code built for it (a
hypothetical caller and request, run nowhere) and what the owner's answers say should happen.

SituationResult.title: SituationResult
SituationResult.description:
What the drafted rules do with a situation (`result`, the kernel's), and whether that matches what was
planned: a plan of `allow_if_reviewed` matches a result that depends on the reviewer, decided by an auto rule
with `review`; any other plan matches the same outcome when it doesn't depend on the reviewer.

StoppedDraft.title: StoppedDraft
StoppedDraft.description:
A reply of Claude's the kernel's reply check stopped (Plan 02b): the draft as the check had it, and each
violation the check found, with the span of the draft it matched (a canary's is "document text", never the canary),
the facts it concerns and the rule that matched. It is the owner's alone: no visitor read or event, no model
context, no reply check, no job and no log line carries it.

Suggestion.title: Suggestion
Suggestion.description:
A rule the owner's own approvals suggest: they approved `count` requests of `tool` in the last 30 days and no
auto card covers it, so `card` would let Claude handle them. `text` is the owner-facing line; on a money tool the
card allows no more than the largest amount approved, and never more than the money cap.

ThisWeek.title: ThisWeek
ThisWeek.description:
"Last 7 days": the seven local dates ending today, in `timezone`. Totals run from 00:00 on `start` to now;
`booked_cents` adds, for each booking, the newest quote of its conversation made at or before it that no earlier
booking took (none: 0); `handled + stepped_in == conversations`; `days` holds all seven, oldest first, the last
one `end`. `stopped` counts refused requests from visitors and agents (owner decision, 2026-10-31).
Safety lists Claude's stopped drafts too, without counting them; the briefing omits them.

Today.title: Today
Today.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/today`, computed from the rows on each read. `live` holds the conversations with
activity in the last 5 minutes; `recorded_history` says which sections count replayed rows.

owner_plain.title: Owner Plain
owner_plain.description: Owner-only kernel reason for an execution refusal, fetched with the owner's credential; null otherwise.

ToolDecisionRow.title: ToolDecisionRow
ToolDecisionRow.description:
One decision on a tool, as its page lists it: whose session asked (`display_name` as `NeedsYouSession`'s,
untrusted when a visitor typed it), the outcome and where the request stands, the kernel's owner text, when it was
decided and its ledger entry. `replayed` is true for a decision from the night the kernel replayed into the copy
(recorded history), and for one whose ledger entry can't be read, which is never shown as live.

ToolDecisions.title: ToolDecisions
ToolDecisions.description:
`GET /api/owner/desks/{desk_id}/tools/{tool}/decisions`: a page of the tool's decisions on the Desk, newest
first; `next_before` is the cursor for the next page, None on the last.

ToolRow.title: ToolRow
ToolRow.description:
A tool of the Desk as the kernel lists it (`kernel_ro.tools`): its effects, whether it can be undone, its
status (`needs_review` until the owner confirms a connected tool), the description Claude sees and, for a
connected tool, the hash of the definition it is pinned to and a changed definition waiting for review; and the
active rules' cards that cover it, default asks included, in card order (Plan 02b, Task 9).

ToolsConfirmIn.title: ToolsConfirmIn
ToolsConfirmIn.description: The shared batch review body; the checked Desk ID comes from the route.

TranscriptItem.title: TranscriptItem
TranscriptItem.description:
One transcript entry as the visitor sees it: their own words, or an event the API delivered or emitted.

`owner_joined` and `owner_left` (Plan 02b) are where the owner took the conversation over and handed it back, each
with the event the visitor's stream got then (`EvOwnerJoined` names the owner as the kernel had them), at that
moment; a resume after a breaker pause has none. A client that doesn't know a kind skips the item.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One or two short, plain sentences for the owner.

category.title: Category
category.description: The subject of the checkpoint event.

Triage.title: Triage
Triage.description:
A checkpoint event, summarized for the owner (route `triage`): what the person asked for and what the Desk
did, and a category for the Safety page's filters. AI-written, for the owner alone.

urgent_when.title: Urgent When
urgent_when.description: When a request is urgent, 1 to 300 characters.

VerifyChecked.title: VerifyChecked
VerifyChecked.description:
`POST /api/public/desks/{slug}/verify/check`: the session as the kernel has it once the code was right, verified
as the contact on record (assurance `demo_code`).

VisitorSession.title: VisitorSession
VisitorSession.description:
`POST /api/public/desks/{slug}/sessions`: the session the visitor cookie now holds, and whether it is the one
the cookie already held (a returning visitor) or a new one.

VisitorTranscript.title: VisitorTranscript
VisitorTranscript.description:
`GET /api/public/desks/{slug}/session`: the session's state, its transcript as the visitor sees it, and the
highest event `seq` read in the same snapshot, which the event stream continues after.

WeekDay.title: WeekDay
WeekDay.description:
One date of "Last 7 days", counted as `ThisWeek` counts: `stopped` counts refused requests that day
(owner decision, 2026-10-31). Claude's stopped drafts are listed on Safety but not counted.

WentLive.title: WentLive
WentLive.description: The Desk answers the public now, at `public_url`.
